metaData.originalTitle: Accelerating LLM-Driven Developer Productivity at Zoox
metaData.title: Accelerating LLM-Driven Developer Productivity at Zoox
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Zoox's AI lead shares a systematic approach to building an enterprise AI platform, Cortex, to accelerate the entire developer lifecycle through secure LLM access, RAG, agentic APIs, and a focus on adoption.
metaData.summary: This presentation details Zoox's journey in building an internal AI platform called Cortex to enhance developer productivity. Amit Navindgi, the lead, outlines the challenges of the developer lifecycle, from information discovery to customer support, and how AI can remove friction. The core of the talk is the platform's architecture: a secure gateway to models like Claude and Gemini, knowledge bases built via RAG from internal sources (Confluence, Slack, GitHub), and an agentic API that allows teams to create custom agents by composing tools. A key innovation is the 'agent as API' paradigm, where teams define tools once in a central registry and invoke agents via REST, separating business logic from platform concerns. The talk also covers critical enterprise features like human-in-the-loop for write actions, managing quotas, and supporting multimodal inputs. Beyond the platform, Navindgi emphasizes the importance of driving adoption through identifying AI champions, building usage dashboards, running hackathons, and creating a culture of sharing wins and failures. He advocates for a pragmatic 'build what you cannot buy' approach, citing the adoption of Cursor over an internal solution. The key takeaway is that a successful AI strategy requires not just building a robust platform but also actively evangelizing its use and measuring its impact.
metaData.featuredReason: Zoox details its strategy for boosting LLM-driven developer productivity through an in-house AI platform, Cortex, and various applications. The presentation covers Cortex's design for security, multi-modality, and tool integration, alongside solutions like Humblebrag and ZI AutoAssist addressing developer pain points. Crucially, Zoox highlights its adoption blueprint, emphasizing AI champions, transparent sharing, and hackathons to drive widespread internal AI tool usage.

mainPoints.point: Build a secure, contributor-friendly platform as the foundation for enterprise AI.
mainPoints.explanation: Zoox built Cortex as a secure gateway to multiple LLMs, with RAG pipelines for internal knowledge and an agentic API. The platform is designed to be extended by any engineer, preventing the core team from becoming a bottleneck.

mainPoints.point: Implement an 'agent as API' paradigm to simplify agent creation and deployment.
mainPoints.explanation: Teams define tools once in a central registry and invoke agents via a REST API, specifying the model, prompt, and tools. This separates business logic from platform concerns like scaling and safety, making agent creation accessible to all teams.

mainPoints.point: Prioritize adoption through evangelism, measurement, and community building.
mainPoints.explanation: Building the platform is only half the battle. Zoox drives adoption by identifying AI champions, building dashboards to track usage and impact, hosting team-specific sessions, and running hackathons to generate excitement and new tools.

mainPoints.point: Adopt a 'build what you cannot buy' strategy and converge later.
mainPoints.explanation: Zoox bought Cursor when it became available, shutting down an internal project. The principle '1 > 2 > 0' allows for temporary duplication to maintain speed, with the goal of converging on the best solution over time.

keyQuotes: When AI is missing, it feels broken.
Build what you cannot buy. If a vendor tool exists that does 80% of what you need, buy it.
1 greater than 2 greater than 0. One good solution is better than two competing ones, but two competing ones are still better than having nothing.
Resist the hype and focus on impact. It is the only way to scale AI inside a company.
If you cannot measure it, you cannot improve it.
